questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When choosing my study destination, I focused on the city's environment, the school's style, and the local lifestyle. The city is safe, comfortable, with convenient transportation and a reasonable cost of living, making it ideal for long-term stay. The school has a diverse teaching style, combining theory with practical experience, and offers numerous international exchange opportunities. The local atmosphere is friendly and open, with a high level of internationalization, allowing me to interact with students from different cultural backgrounds and broaden my horizons.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Yes, the school provided comprehensive information through both emails and the official website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I arrived at the school, I received a freshman gift pack, which contained many useful information booklets and practical items, including a campus map, a local life guide and a list of procedures that needed to be completed, which gave me a clear understanding of what I needed to deal with next.

Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Directly assigned to a student dormitory

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Student dormitories provide communal kitchens

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You should contact the Student Services Center in advance to ask them to help arrange student dormitories.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First, you need to sign a student insurance contract before departure, then you need to pay a student union service fee, and finally you just need to go to the campus to get your student card to automatically complete the registration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Ask questions and get answers via email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I signed up for most of the classes I wanted to take, although I later changed them due to time conflicts.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the instructions in the email and plan the courses you want to take in advance. If you encounter any problems, you can contact the coordinator by email. They are very enthusiastic to help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses related to my major are all at the MA level. Some elective courses have no level restrictions.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There will be more students in the class, and the courses and exams will be more difficult.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Clinical Applications of Computational Medicine.
This course has a high degree of freedom. It is a project-oriented course. Students complete projects through group collaboration, and will cooperate with laboratories or even hospitals, which gives them a lot of room for creativity.

questions.answer: I don't participate in many non -academic activities, so I can't recommend them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You can take a train to hike near the Alps, where there are beautiful snow-capped mountains and lakes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult for me because I am not very sociable and I don't speak German.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Germans love hiking, so I was inspired by it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The pressure from exams and studies will become greater, so please be prepared.
You can get a tick vaccine.
Don't have too much hope for DB Railway to be on time, and be prepared for 100% delays.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think it was those unforgettable hiking experiences, and being deeply moved by the beautiful scenery of the mountains in southern Germany.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I need to take more than four exams at the same time during the final exam, as well as other projects, so it is necessary to plan your time well.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
